memo.verdict: Neutral; park at the current price; conviction medium. Bullish on the business, neutral on the shares. The case is parked on the return and the riskiness, not on any gate: no D or F sits on management (B), business quality (C), predictability (C) or trackability (B). It re-opens on price, near EUR 3.00 (the eighteen-month entry level; EUR 2.45 for the three-year horizon), or on evidence that moves the multiple argument; a European clearance by 26 November 2026 with at most one vessel remedy and a FY2027 EBITDA guide at or above EUR 2.1bn in February 2027 would lift the blend toward 12x, which at consensus earnings is still only about +7 percent a year at eighteen months from today's price, so the price, not the news, is what would re-open the case. Not invalidated.
case: - The thesis: Saipem is a repaired cyclical with a corporate event attached: a fully booked deepwater fleet in the strongest offshore sanctioning cycle since 2013, a nil-premium merger with Subsea 7 awaiting European clearance, and a lease book that starts to roll off in 2027. At EUR 4.322 the shares already pay for the cycle, the FY2027 margin step and the merger; on an earnings footing the stock sits at the top of its peers, so the modal return is negative over eighteen months and about nil over three years. The business case is compelling; the investment case is not, at this price.

- The change that matters is external and cyclical: offshore sanctioning capital spending from USD 115bn (2026) to USD 149bn (2027), the highest since 2013, greenfield share rising to 71% by 2028, tier-one fleets booked through 2027 to 2028, deepwater breakevens of USD 35 to 44 per barrel against Brent about USD 70. It is cyclical with a plateau named after 2028. It reaches Saipem through price and mix, not volume, because the fleet is already 100% booked for 2026 and 2027: contract rates +3% to 5%, day rates +5% to 7%, capacity into 2028 and 2029 at premium terms. 'External forces' B; 'Demand' B; 'Supply side' B (the vessel scarcity is Saipem's asset; the costs are 18-to-24-month component lead times, labour shortages and Hormuz logistics); 'Competition' C (a three-player core with firm pricing; tightening at the edges in Brazil and onshore; TechnipFMC taking 80% of intake by direct award); 'Own cycle' C (mid-to-late; backlog down from EUR 31,120m to EUR 29,861m; revenue growth from +22.5% to +6.5% to +1.9%; the turn ahead is in intake).

- The internal change is mostly delivered: chief executive since 31 August 2022; "value over volume"; shallow-water drilling sold to ADES for USD 285m; the Thai Oil Clean Fuel contract terminated; legacy zero-margin projects from seven to two; a EUR 104m redundancy programme; dividends reinstated with a floor of at least 40% of free cash flow after leases; gross debt reduced; red-flag check clean. The screen's rule (three forces strong, or chief-executive change plus a guidance increase) is met only by the historical record, and the year's guidance move was a cut. 'Internal forces' C; the merger ('Acquisitions' B) is the one large internal force still ahead; 'Guidance raised' D.
counter_case: - The strongest case against the record's view is the sell-side's: eight of thirteen brokers at buy or overweight, a mean target of EUR 4.89 and a top of EUR 6.00. The right lens is enterprise value to EBITDA, on which Saipem at 3.8x FY2027 (before leases) sits at a 38% discount to its own upcycle average and far below Subsea 7 (about 5.8x) and TechnipFMC (about 12.9x), because lease depreciation overstates economic depreciation and the tax rate normalises. Free cash flow after leases of EUR 600m, rising toward EUR 700m to 800m as leases fall, gives a 7% to 11% yield that compounds into a 55% cumulative return by 2030. Consensus FY2027 to FY2028 earnings are themselves too low, because cost recovery (EUR 70m), the drilling recovery and EUR 300m of synergies (8.8% of combined EBITDA) are not in them. A cleared Saipem7 is the global leader of a market with no new supply to 2028 and deserves at least Subsea 7's multiple on those higher earnings, which gives EUR 5.50 to 6.00 and 20 percent-plus a year. The evidence for it is real: cash conversion has beaten every forecast, order intake is running 27% above expectations, and the balance sheet is the sector's strongest.

- Conceded: on the free-cash-flow lens the shares are fairly valued rather than dear (EUR 3.70 to 4.30 at an 8% yield); the merger adds quality at nil premium and 12.3x is a defensible ceiling for the cleared branch (+0.4 percent a year at eighteen months); cost recovery is upside the price does not carry; the record's FY2027 EBITDA may be EUR 60m too low.
triggers: - The price: progress the case if the shares fall toward EUR 3.00 (eighteen-month entry) or EUR 2.45 (three-year entry). Alarm on the multiple above 14x the record's earnings (about EUR 4.70); below 8x with earnings intact (about EUR 2.40) is the entry, not an invalidation.

- The European Commission's Phase 2 decision by 26 November 2026, either way: clearance with at most one or two vessel remedies and closing by mid-2027 is the record's modal (about 75%); remedies named or a decision deferred into 2027 is the alarm; prohibition, or remedies above two rigid pipelay vessels, invalidates the merger driver. A clearance with at most one vessel remedy plus a FY2027 guide at or above EUR 2.1bn lifts the blend toward 12x.

- Q3 2026 results on 18 November 2026: H2 transit costs below EUR 70m and a reported Asset Based Services margin at or above 17% would change the record's mind on FY2027 EBITDA; H2 cost above EUR 80m is the alarm; a further guidance cut, or recovery below 50% refused in writing, invalidates the cost-normalisation driver. Any further FY2026 guidance move is a re-run trigger.
- FY2026 results in February 2027 with the FY2027 guide: at or above EUR 2.1bn changes the record's mind; below 12% margin is the alarm; FY2027 EBITDA below EUR 1,850m invalidates the margin driver.
- Cost recovery: a signed variation order, or a fourth quarter of EUR 70m of transit cost, would change the view; no recovery agreement by Q2 2027 is the alarm.

- Intake: FY2026 intake above EUR 13bn is the modal; below EUR 13bn the alarm; below EUR 11bn, or the 2027 sanctioning forecast cut below USD 130bn, invalidates the cycle driver. Sanctioning forecasts for 2028 to 2029 rising rather than flattening would argue against the modelled de-rating.
